chunks: 458 - Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Wahb ibn Hafas, from Abu Basir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, the Qa'im (peace be upon him) will have his name announced on the night of the 23rd, and he will rise (reappear) on the day of Ashura, on which al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them) was martyred."

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Riser/Reariser, a title for Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.)
key_terms.صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ: Peace and blessings of God upon him
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ ثَلَاثٍ وَعِشْرِينَ: The night of the 23rd (of the month of Ramadan)
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَاشُورَاءَ: The day of Ashura (10th of Muharram)

ai.seo_question: When will Imam Mahdi (a.s.) rise and what is the significance of the date?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) in *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the profound symbolic timing of the Mahdi's emergence, linking his proclamation on the 23rd night to his actual rising on Ashura, the day of Imam Husayn’s martyrdom. This connection underscores the concept of *tawassul* through the Ahl al-Bayt, suggesting that the Mahdi’s victory completes the narrative of his grandfather’s sacrifice. The specific mention of the 23rd night often invites scholarly discussion regarding its relation to the lunar calendar and the timing of the call (*al-nida'*).
